story: Gary heads off toward the Rec Center on Magnolia Loop, eager to get to his pickleball game on this sunny Halloween afternoon. Donna is busy hiding all but three of the pink plastic flamingos behind the hedge, while Hal stands nearby with his notebook, sternly tallying each one that's still visible from the street. Rosa, cheerful as ever, thanks Gary for his offer to help with her porch later and asks him to pass along word that hot cider is waiting on her porch after the parade.
events: Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving only three visible from the street
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and record the tally in my notebook

gary.thought_process: Donna's calling me to court one, and Hal's already over at her flamingos with his notebook. Rosa's invited me to her porch tonight, which warms me up. I said my hellos to Rosa last tick, so no need to repeat the toolbox pitch. The cart lights and sound system are for the parade at 6, and I have a pending application at the architectural review desk, but that can wait an hour. Donna's been patient and our two hours on the court are ticking. I should answer her, accept Rosa's invite, and head to the rec center.

parameters.content: Heading to the pickleball court with Donna for drills; I'll swing by Rosa's porch tonight after the parade.

donna.thought_process: I told Gary at tick 288 that the court was waiting and we'd drill, and he answered Rosa instead, so I shouldn't nag him again. Hal is counting the flamingos for his notebook, and I promised him I'd pull the extras behind the hedge so the street stays tidy. L-02 says no more than 3 ornaments visible from the street, so I need to get on that before parade day. Quick fix, then I can collect Gary and head to the courts.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving only three visible from the street

hal.thought_process: I'm standing on Magnolia Loop with the flamingo flock in plain view. Donna's headed to the court with Gary, so I won't have her cornered long. My goal is the tally for the committee report, and L-02 caps visible ornaments at three. Count them now, write it down, and let the notebook do the talking. Halloween parade is tonight, so the report should be tidy before the street fills up.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and record the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: Treats are bagged and my evening is clear. I already invited everyone to my porch last tick, and Gary offered to help, so I shouldn't repeat myself. Donna is hustling Gary off to the courts and Hal is counting flamingos. My bigger goal is getting all three neighbors at one table, and Halloween night with the cart parade is a natural chance. I'll warmly acknowledge Gary's offer, then let them get on with their afternoon. A quick specific nudge to Donna and Hal about coming by my porch after the parade keeps things moving forward without repeating the same line.

parameters.content: Thanks, Gary, I'll take you up on that porch help later. Go win your pickleball, and tell Donna and Hal there's hot cider on my porch after the parade.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
